candidates.headline: Top Programmers Return to Hand-Coding Amid AI Tool Doubts
candidates.excerpt: Senior developers abandoning AI coding assistants and returning to manual coding practices due to reliability and quality concerns.
candidates.comedy_angle: The irony of AI hype cycles: expensive tools promise to replace developers, but experts reject them and code by hand anyway—a perfect setup for Cody's 'AI solves nothing' bit.

candidates.headline: AI slop videos aimed at babies are 'garbage,' says pediatrician
candidates.excerpt: Medical professionals warn that AI-generated content targeting infants is low-quality and potentially harmful to child development.
candidates.comedy_angle: AI companies optimizing for engagement over ethics, now targeting the one demographic that can't complain—babies. Sakura's 'AI ethics theater' angle.

candidates.headline: Claude Opus 4.6 vs. Opus 4.7 Effort Levels and Prompt Steering Benchmarks
candidates.excerpt: Detailed benchmark comparison of Anthropic's latest Claude models showing marginal improvements and effort-level trade-offs.
candidates.comedy_angle: Incremental version bumps with marginal gains—the AI industry's version of smartphone releases where the only difference is the camera.

candidates.headline: Has AI Changed the Course of Drug Development? Three Years Later
candidates.excerpt: Analysis of AI's actual impact on pharmaceutical R&D three years into the hype cycle, with sobering reality checks.
candidates.comedy_angle: AI promised to revolutionize drug discovery; three years later, reality is messier. Perfect for Deep's 'AI overpromise' segment.

candidates.headline: Why Every AI-Coded App Is an Island
candidates.excerpt: Technical analysis of why AI-generated code creates isolated, non-interoperable systems that can't integrate with existing infrastructure.
candidates.comedy_angle: AI code is siloed and incompatible—ironic given the industry's promise of seamless automation and integration.

candidates.headline: Hash anchors and Myers diff and single-token anchors: 60% cheaper AI code edits
candidates.excerpt: Technical optimization reducing the cost of AI-assisted code editing by 60% through novel anchor and diff strategies.
candidates.comedy_angle: Engineers obsessing over micro-optimizations to make AI tools slightly less expensive—a niche technical win that won't change the fundamental problems.

candidates.headline: Ask HN: Where are all the consumer ChatGPT apps?
candidates.excerpt: Community discussion questioning why consumer-facing ChatGPT applications remain sparse despite years of hype.
candidates.comedy_angle: ChatGPT promised to be everywhere; instead, it's mostly a web tab. The app ecosystem never materialized—classic AI hype gap.

candidates.headline: Ask HN: How I find a job where what is needed is solid code, not firefighting?
candidates.excerpt: Developer seeking employment where quality engineering matters more than crisis management and technical debt patching.
candidates.comedy_angle: The AI industry's dirty secret: even with 'productivity tools,' engineers still spend most time fixing broken systems instead of building.

candidates.headline: Octopal: Powerful AI agents without blind trust
candidates.excerpt: New AI agent framework emphasizing transparency and control over black-box automation.
candidates.comedy_angle: Yet another AI agent tool claiming to solve trust issues—the same promise every startup makes before users realize they still don't understand what it's doing.

candidates.headline: Show HN: Are AI competitor newsletters useful?
candidates.excerpt: New newsletter product analyzing the utility and market saturation of AI industry competitive intelligence newsletters.
candidates.comedy_angle: Meta: a newsletter about whether AI newsletters are useful. The AI industry eating its own tail in real time.
